page: Microsoft Azure E16_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Operating under the x86_64 architecture on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs provisioned across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 128.0 GB, establishing a substantial 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware vector and cryptographical capabilities include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES-NI, backed by 35 MB of shared L3 cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core. The instance includes zero local disk storage and contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight solid mid-tier multi-threaded and memory performance paired with constrained single-thread execution. The instance recorded an average multi-core score of 14807.48 on stress-ng and 7581.0 on Geekbench, whereas single-core stress-ng performance scored 1411.28, falling into the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth remains competitive, achieving 83.97 GB/sec uncached read throughput and 45.84 GB/sec uncached write throughput. Application-level metrics reflect these memory dynamics, reaching 14.0 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.13 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Machine learning inference on a 7B model achieved 22.92 tokens per second for prompt processing, demonstrating lower-tier throughput for complex language tasks.

With its 1:8 core-to-memory ratio and reliance on network-attached storage, the E16_v4 is economically suited for enterprise workloads constrained by memory capacity rather than core compute cycles. Primary workload targets include in-memory data stores such as Redis, enterprise relational databases, distributed analytics engines, and memory-heavy application servers. Organizations requiring intensive per-core speed or local high-speed temporary storage may find the architecture less cost-effective due to single-thread limitations and the absence of ephemeral disks.
description: Microsoft Azure E16_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine offering 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Built on an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V, the platform utilizes 8 physical cores with hyperthreading and includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 extensions. The server is diskless, containing no local ephemeral storage or integrated GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance displays middle-tier multi-core compute and robust memory bandwidth, evidenced by 83.97 GB/sec uncached reads and 14.0 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, though single-core execution sits in the lower performance quartile. The configuration is best matched for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational databases, caching layers, and analytical workloads where large RAM capacity is the critical operating factor.
